title: Pulse Quality Optimisation in Quantum Optimal Control
summary: Quantum optimal control methods are widely used to design experimental control pulses such as laser amplitudes, phases, or detunings, that implement a target unitary evolution. In practice, what makes a pulse "good" depends not only on its fidelity, but also on the experimental setting and the relevant hardware constraints. Here, we introduce geometric quantum control with kernel optimisation (GECKO), a model-agnostic method for improving control pulses after a high-fidelity solution has been found.
